chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Miskan from Is'haq al-Fazari who said:

He was asked, and I was in his presence, meaning Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), about a newborn who was born neither male nor female, and had only a backside (no front). How would he inherit? He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Imam sits, and people sit with him, so he supplicates to Allah and casts the lots to determine upon which inheritance he would inherit: the inheritance of the male or the inheritance of the female? So whichever of those comes out, he inherits according to it.'

Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'And which judgment is more just than a judgment determined by casting lots? Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "So he drew lots (with them), so he was of those who are cast off."'
ai.seo_question: How is inheritance determined for a hermaphrodite with only a backside according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the juristic procedure for determining the inheritance share of a hermaphrodite (dhaw al-dhabr) possessing only a posterior opening, utilizing a ritual of supplication and casting lots (al-jiyal bi-l-sihham) to assign either male or female status. The Imam cites the Quranic narrative of Prophet Yunus to validate this method of divine decision-making, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on using lot-casting as a legitimate mechanism for resolving legal ambiguity in inheritance cases.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazal Bin Shazaan and Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Is’haq Al Fazary who said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> was asked and I was in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, meaning Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, about the birth of a child and not being with a male part nor a femal part, and there was not for him except for a backside. How would he inherit?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Imam<sup>asws</sup> would be seated in a gathering, and the people would be seated along with him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> would supplicate to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and would make the drawing of the lots upon which inheritance it would inherit, the inheritance of the male or the inheritance of the female? So whichever of that comes out, it would inherit upon it’.

Then heasws said: ‘And which judgement is more just than a judgement made upon it by the drawing of the lots. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [37:141] So he drew lots (with them), so he was of those who are cast off’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al- Jabbar all from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Ishaq al-Fazariy who has narrated the following: “

Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked, when I was with him, about the case of a newborn who is not a male or female but there is only the anus and how to deal with the inheritance of such person. He (the Imam) said, ‘The Imam and people come in a gathering, pray to Allah then arrange a raffle to see the name of which sex comes and deal with the case according to the result of the raffle.
No other means is as fair as raffle; Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, ‘They cast raffle and he lost in the raffle.’” [37:141]
